recipes.name: Turkey Veggie Meatloaf Cups
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup barbecue sauce, or as needed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Spray 20 muffin cups with cooking spray.

Place zucchini, onions, and red bell pepper into a food processor, and pulse several times until finely chopped but not liquefied. Place the vegetables into a bowl and mix in ground turkey, couscous, egg, Worcestershire sauce, and Dijon mustard until thoroughly combined.
Fill each prepared muffin cup about 3/4 full. Top each cup with about 1 teaspoon of barbecue sauce.

Bake in the preheated oven until juices run clear, about 25 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of muffins should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Turkey Veggie Meatloaf Cups
raw_recipe.description: These meatloaf cups are made with ground turkey, couscous, zucchini, onion, and bell pepper. Make perfect individual servings with this easy recipe.

video.description: Lightly-seasoned ground turkey is mixed with couscous for a real protein punch. These deliciously adorable meatloaf cups are baked in cupcake tins for a personalized meal!

review.reviewBody:
This is our latest favourite recipe. I freeze the uncooked meatloaf cups by scooping generous scoops and pressing them onto parchment paper covered cookie sheets. Freeze on the cookie sheet, then package in ziploc bags. Now, we've got fast food potential!
I agree about adding garlic. You can also disguise/dress them up by shaping the small tortilla shells into muffin tins and cooking them at 350 for ten minutes. Plunk a meatloaf cup into each, and your meal looks even more appealing.

I normally don’t modify the first time I make a dish, but I wanted additional servings. So I bought 1 pound of ground turkey breast, and 1.17 pounds of dark ground turkey. When I get home with the meat and read through some of the reviews, and I see the notes that there are too many veggies in the recipe. So my modifications are not really with the ingredients, but with the amounts, and it turned out great. I did add spices. Based on other reviews, I hand-diced my veggies instead of using my food processor. The end result was that I was able to fill 24 standard muffin cups almost to the top, using 75 g of mixture per cup, and then topping off with 1 TBL of sauce. Additionally, I had a small 6“ x 8“ aluminum pan from Maggiano’s leftovers, and was able to fill it about the same thickness/depth as a muffin cup. All cooked for about 22 min to doneness. Basically 2x meat, couscous, eggs, and the flavor sauces with 1.5x vegs. Here are my ingredient amounts: a little more than 3 cups/420g of diced zucchini, 1 large onion 377g chopped after peeling, 1 large red bell pepper 180g after seeding, 2.17 lbs meat, 1 cup/130g of uncooked couscous, 2 large eggs, 5 TBL/84 g of Worcestershire sauce, 2 TBL/40g Dijon mustard, PLUS 7g Penney’s Cajun Spice & 1/2 tsp salt. I only had thin Eastern Carolina vinegar barbecue sauce (240g), so I thickened it up by adding ketchup (150g) and Hoisin sauce (60g). Calories = 91 per muffin cup

So good! I didn't have couscous so used 1 cup of cooked quinoa that I'd made with chicken stock. After mixing everything, I taste-tested a teeny patty that I microwaved and ended up adding 6 cloves of minced garlic and 1.25 tsp of fine sea salt. The patty also wasn't holding together so I added an extra egg. I filled the muffin cups the entire way and it made 18 muffins. They cooked within 30 minutes and held together. I made my own spicy BBQ sauce with 1/2 cup sugar-free ketchup, 3 TBs maple syrup, 1 TBs apple cider vinegar, 1/2 tsp cayenne, 1/2 tsp garlic powder and 1/4 tsp onion powder. This one is going on the regular rotation. Thanks so much for the recipe, Amy!

This was a very kid friendly dish. It passed the toddler test. It never occurred to me to use zucchini in meatloaf. I might start adding it to my beef meal loaf too. I used 1 tablespoon of dried onion flakes instead of fresh onion. Did not use pepper because I didn't have one in the fridge. Instead of couscous, I used 1/4 cup rolled oats. I defrosted grated zucchini. I was surprised at how much it shrank while cooking but the result was very dense, filling and moist. I might add another egg to make up for missing pepper next time.

This recipe is a staple in our home....but my first time I made it, it was very watery/mushy. Since then, I've been cutting the vegetables in the morning and putting them on a paper towel to pull the water out. It's made a huge difference! No more mushy meatloaf! Delicious ??

This is a great recipe! It's relatively easy, makes a lot, freezes and reheats well, and tastes great to be so low calorie. I did change it up a bit though to fit my flavor preferences. I used 1.5-2 cups of canned sweet potato instead of zucchini. I left the onions and bell pepper coarsely diced for texture. And I added some freshly ground black pepper, garlic salt, parsley, and a pinch of cayenne for flavor. It came out perfectly! I served it with sautéed green beans and homemade mashed potatoes and it felt very hearty and filling even though the whole meal was less than 400 calories. The idea of making it muffin cups is genius! Easy to cook, portion, serve, and store.

Good recipe. The first time I made it, I followed the recipe exactly and it was a little plain. Probably because of the BBQ sauce I used. The next time, I made a tangy sweet sauce with chili sauce and crushed pineapple instead. It was a hit!

After reading multiple reviews, I reduced the amount of veggies, but apparently not enough, because the mix was still rather runny and I was unable to form this into a "loaf" like I had planned. I also added quite a few different spices and herbs to the mix along with minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Next time around, I will further decrease the amount of veggies so I can actually form a loaf with the mix, but otherwise, it was quite tasty the way I modified the recipe. Here's what I added in the way of seasoning: 1 tsp each salt, fresh ground pepper, lemon pepper, dried basil, and dried parsley; 1 cube beef bullion; 1/8 tsp each cumin, cayenne, and dried red pepper flakes.

We’ve been trying to eat a more clean diet so this recipe caught my eye. It was easy to make and came out great. I did substitute 1/4 cup cooked quinoa for the couscous. I made them in the big muffin tin and it made 6. They were gone in two days and my husband asked me to make more right away. I only used one pound of ground turkey; I may try 1.5 pounds next time. While they did stand up fine, the texture was a little soft for my taste.

I did make these muffin cups and my husband loved them. Instead of 1/2 cup couscous I added a package of NEar East mushroom couscous (seasoning packet and couscous). I also added a head of roasted garlic & 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese. They were moist and delicious. Will be making them again.

Very good. I added the 1/2 C of barbecue sauce directly into the mixture vs. on top of the muffins and I actually filled the entire muffin cups for a little larger portion and kept the cook time the same, it worked out great. Put 2 each in freezer bags, we'll use them for breakfasts.
This recipe offers a straightforward preparation process, resulting in a remarkably moist and flavorful outcome.

Thank you, great substitute for low fat diet. This turned out fantastic, few subs had to do with what had on hand, ground chicken was used, cooked quinoa, and seasoned with kinders buttery onion and buttery herb and a bit of quick oats as I also halved the veggies as suggested by others for extra binding. The BBQ sauce really takes this to another level. Adding this to the notation!
Our family loves this recipe.

I loved the recipe. I don’t like the texture of couscous, so I substituted it with partially cooked rice. The small cups are easy portions to take for my lunch and for freezing for a later day. I’ll definitely share this recipe.
Pretty good stuff. Moist.
Needs more bbq sauce, but that was about it. My grandma loved them.
Amazing! I made modifications that others suggested like garlic and salt/pepper. I will make it again.

Meh. This came out watery and not very tasty. I was looking for a healthier version of the turkey meatballs we usually make (with breadcrumbs and parmesan) but nope. Just a disappointed kiddo at dinner, and I had to agree that it wasn't very yummy.

These were very flavorful. I used quinoa instead of couscous which I’m not sure was the right thing to do. They didn’t hold together as well as they would have. Otherwise, they were good. The BBQ sauce makes a nice topping.
